newsitem.title: USA: Adoption agency bilked dozens, New York suit says.
newsitem.headline: Adoption agency bilked dozens, New York suit says.

text.p: A New York adoption agency charged would-be parents exorbitant fees but never delivered the babies, New York State alleged in a lawsuit filed Thursday.

"Families go through a great deal of emotional and financial stress when searching for a child to adopt and are especially vulnerable to greedy con-artists like these," said New York State Attorney General Dennis Vacco.

Vacco's lawsuit, filed in Manhattan State Supreme Court, accuses Today's Adoption Agency and its directors of collecting thousands of dollars from dozens of prospective adoptive parents who were never given a child. Vacco said the couples "were left with nothing but broken hearts."
Vacco said he is seeking to shut down the Port Jervis, New York-based agency and to force its directors, Patricia Zuvic, Denise Zuvic and Stanley B. Michelman, to pay refunds to the couples.
According to the lawsuit, Today's Adoption promised couples that they would get them foreign-born children from Guatemala and Paraguay for fees ranging from $9,000 to over $30,000 in one case.
The adoption agency did not return calls for comment.
